chunks: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who swears an oath but then sees that leaving it is better, and if he does not leave it he fears he may be sinning — should he leave it?
So he (peace be upon him) said: Have you not heard the saying of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family): 'When you see something better than your oath, then leave it'?

key_terms.أَفْضَلُ: Better/preferable (afdal); the comparative form indicating a more virtuous course of action
key_terms.الْيَمِينُ: Oath/sworn vow (yamin); in Islamic law, a binding verbal commitment sworn by God's name
key_terms.فَدَعْهَا: Leave it/abandon it (fada'ha); the imperative form of wada'a meaning to set aside or forgo
key_terms.يَأْثَمَ: To sin/incur sin (ya'thama); committing a morally prohibited act

ai.seo_question: What should a Muslim do if they swear an oath but later see that breaking it would be better?
ai.summary: Sa'id al-A'raj asked Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about someone caught between keeping an oath and doing what is better, fearing sin either way. The Imam answered by citing a prophetic hadith: when one sees a better course of action than what was sworn, one should abandon the oath. This teaching reflects the Islamic legal principle that oaths are not to be used as chains preventing one from doing good, and the expiation (kaffarah) covers the breaking of such an oath.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali Bin Al Noman, from Saeed Al A’raj who said, 
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who swore an oath, so he saw that leaving it is better, and if he were not to leave it, he feared that he might be sinning. Should he leave it?’
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Have you not heard the words of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>: ‘When you see better than what you had oathed for, so leave it’?’
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ali ibn al-Nu’man from Sa‘id al-A‘raj who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who vows to do a certain thing then finds out that not doing it is better, and if he did not disregard it he is afraid of committing a sin; if he can disregard it.

He (the Imam) said, ‘Have you not heard the words of the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, “If you find something better than that for which you have taken an oath you can disregard it.’””
